Careers Education
At Lord Williams's School, we provide students with comprehensive careers information, advice and guidance to prepare them for their next steps into further education and their future careers. We seek to raise their aspirations and make them aware of all the options and opportunities available to them. The Careers team is committed to promoting equality, celebrating diversity and challenging stereotypes.
The Careers team is based in the KS4 Library Block. Our Careers Lead is Mr Gareth Roberts who has responsibility for the design and co-ordination of a comprehensive and relevant careers programme for all students. Our Careers and Work Experience co-ordinator is Mrs Emma Spink. For 1-1 careers advice, students from Year 7 upwards can book appointments with the school’s independent Careers adviser via their tutor.
Named Trustee with Responsibility for Careers: Mr Simon Whitfield
The school works in close partnership with local businesses, colleges and universities who attend events to prepare students for the world of work. These include the very successful careers evening, Future Fest and work experience placements for all Year 10 students.
Careers Lead: Gareth Roberts E-mail address: g.roberts@lordwilliams.oxon.sch.uk Telephone number: 01844 210510
'Lord Williams's is committed to supporting its students as they begin to plan their futures beyond school. It actively engages with the local community to enable students of all ages to explore the choices of careers that are open to them. It also explains the range of routes available to help them achieve their ambitions in the way that is best suited to them as individuals.
The dedicated careers department ensures that work experience is available to all students. It also organises a broad range of activities, talks and tuition sessions to extend their knowledge, as well as one-to-one discussions with careers advisors. It is an impressive service. Simon Whitfield, Vice Chair of Trustees

pageCache.text:
SEND Information Report
This report sets out information about our provision for students with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). This information is updated annually.
About our School
Lord Williams’s School, on two separate sites in Thame, provides for students with a wide range of special educational needs, including those with:
The above four SEND categories are definitions of special educational need found in the August 2014 Code of Practice.
We are a mainstream school with Communication and Interaction Resource Bases on each mainstream school site, which cater for up to 22 students with autism spectrum condition.
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Robin Whitby, Assistant Headteacher. He can be contacted via SENDCO@lordwilliams.oxon.sch.uk or 01844 210510.
Our governor with responsibility for SEND is: Rachel Barnard
Our SEN policy can be found here on the Lord Williams’s School website: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) | Lord Williams's School
Our Equality Scheme and Accessibility Plan can be found here on the Lord Williams’s School website: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) | Lord Williams's School
Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs
How do we identify and give extra help to students with SEND?
The school uses Oxfordshire County Council’s guidance ‘Identifying and supporting Special Educational Needs in Oxfordshire schools and settings’.
The guidance sets out:
Please click here to read Oxfordshire County Council's guidance.
For details of how we review data on students, link with students, parents/carers and primary/other schools, please click here for our Assessment Policy.
How do we work with parents/carers and students?
We will always contact parents/carers if we have a concern that their child may have a special educational need.
We work closely with students with SEND and their parent/carers to agree outcomes, how we will all work towards these and then to review progress. We do this via: termly meetings between keyworkers and students (minutes sent home in a SEN Support Plan), EHCP Annual Reviews, additional meetings by arrangement phone calls and email contact when appropriate.
There are also opportunities for parents/carers and students to contribute to our policies on SEND and Equality. We do this by:
Inviting feedback on school website
Opportunities for School Council
Adapting the curriculum
We offer a broad and balanced curriculum for all students including those with SEND. Details are published on the school website and can be found here.
The way we adapt this for students with SEN and disabled students is set out in the school’s Accessibility Policy.
We use a range of intervention programmes to accelerate student progress from Year 7 to Year 11 and 13.
For some identified students we offer opportunities on specialist courses for young people from Year 9 onwards in association with Meadowbrook College, Oxford, Blueprint, Aylesbury, Trax, Oxford and Aylesbury Motor Project and inourelement.org.uk.
What expertise can we offer?
All staff within the Learning Support Faculty have had training at county and national level, on a variety of topics that affect children with special educational needs, including conditions affecting current students in School. These staff lead on training all members of staff to develop inclusion at Lord Williams School.
The SEND staff team have expertise in a variety of areas. The team have a wide range of qualifications including MA (Education), a Post Graduate Certificate in Literacy Learning Difficulties, Post Graduate Certificate in Advanced Educational Practice, a SpLD Assessment Practice Certificate and AMBDA Certification, Post Graduate Diploma in Specific Learning Difficulties and a Certificate in Psychometric Testing, Assessment and Access Arrangements (CPT3A); on the BPS Register of Qualifications in Test Use, ADG-Associate Member of Dyslexia Guild and the NASENCO.
All teaching and support staff have received training in Quality First Teaching to meet the needs of all learners, delivered in partnership with the Oxfordshire Inclusion Team and the Education Psychology team. This training is ongoing as part of the school professional learning plan.
From the attached Communication and Interaction Resource Bases, Teachers and Teaching Assistants provide expertise to mainstream staff, including SEND staff, for continuous awareness of and development of professional skills in working with students with ASD/C.
We acknowledge that part of staff training will come from listening to and working closely with parents/carers and listening to students and value their input to regular review meetings to keep our information sharing about learners up to date.
We also have access to a range of specialist support services including:
We also work with other services and organisations that are involved with a family, with the family’s permission. We always discuss the involvement of specialist SEN services with parents/carers first.
Information about these services and what they offer can be found on the Oxfordshire County Council SEN web pages by clicking here.
Educational Psychology
Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
Oxfordshire Schools Inclusion Team
Various NHS therapy services
The Local Community Support Services
Children’s Social Care
Hospital School
School Nurse
School Counsellors
How do we know if SEN provision is effective?
The progress of all students is tracked throughout the school through teachers’ progress reviews, three times each year. Student progress is also monitored by the SEND team, who analyse progress data.
In addition, we regularly review progress towards agreed outcomes assessing whether the support that has been in place has made a difference and what we need to do next. SEND Support Plans are reviewed three times each year, to determine progress made towards individualised targets. This forms part of the Assess, Plan, Do, Review process.
When we run special intervention programmes for groups of students we assess how successful they have been and use that information to decide on how best to continue with support in the future, this is analysed by the SENDCO and Assistant SENDCOs on a regular basis.
Information about how the Governing Body evaluates the success of the education that is provided for students with SEN is contained in the annual Governors’ SEN Report.
How are children and young people with SEN helped to access activities outside of the classroom?
All students are included in activities and trips (with risk assessments, where needed) and in accordance with duties under the Equalities Act 2010. We talk to parents/carers and students when planning trips so that everyone is clear about what will happen and offer support when needed.
There is information about activities and events for disabled children and those with SEN in Oxfordshire in the Family Information Directory by clicking here.
Oxfordshire’s accessibility strategy can be read here.
What do we do to support the wellbeing of children/young people with SEN?
All students have the opportunity to share their views through
We take bullying very seriously, and monitor incidents on bullying according to Protected Characteristics, including disability related discrimination.
School Council representatives
Joining the school and moving on
We encourage all new prospective students and parents/carers to visit the school before starting. For students with SEND we:
We begin to prepare students for transition into the next stage of their education or training in a number of ways:
For students joining Lord Williams’s School during the final half term of Year 9 it is sometimes advisable to avoid the extra transition from Lower School to Upper School, depending upon the nature of the SEND present. On occasion, school therefore implements plans and provisions to educate these students at the Upper School.
Through an annual Careers Convention (Future Fest)
Who to contact
If you are concerned about your child please contact the Learning Support Faculty via 01844 210510. We will then be able to pass you on to the correct person, who manages your child's provision.
If you would like to provide feedback to us about SEND provision, please contact the SENDCO or Assistant SENDCO for KS3/KS4.
Impartial advice and support on all issues affecting students’ education, including SEND provision, is given by Oxfordshire’s SENDIASS service, who can be contacted by clicking here.
If you would like to know more about opportunities for children and young people with SEN and their families, support groups or information about SEN these are listed in the Family Information Directory
Oxfordshire’s ‘Local Offer’ contains lots of information for parents/carers.
Our school has contributed to the County’s ‘Local Offer’ through attendance at training workshops and through trialling of new guidance and systems.
The Department for Education has published Special Educational Needs and Disability: A guide for parents and carers. It addresses a range of issues.
Robin Whitby, Assistant Headteacher – SENDCo (Designated Teacher for Looked After Children)

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
Welcome to details relating to the work of the Learning Support Faculty at Lord Williams's School.
The following linked pages offer an overview of the people within and work of the Faculty that manages students with a special educational need and/or disability (SEND):
Lord Williams’s is a fully comprehensive school, committed to addressing the needs of all our students, including SEND students - whether this relates to learning, emotional and/or social difficulties, medical or physical disabilities. We work closely with a range of professionals outside school to provide informed pastoral support and support for learning based on students’ specific, individual needs.
There are Learning Support bases on each mainstream school site, well resourced by specialist teachers and teaching assistants. Inclusion and integration are important to us and students are taught in mainstream classes wherever possible. But where more individualised teaching is required, this is usually led by Learning Support teachers and teaching assistants.
Students who have specific language and/or communication needs, that result in a diagnosis of Asperger's Syndrome and/or Autism or similar condition, can be considered for a place at the Communication and Interaction Base. There is a purpose-built Base on each school site. Admission to a Base placement is only through successful Local Authority application and is usually for students who have been supported in specialist provision during their primary school years. Students will require a Statement of Educational Needs or an Education, Health and Care Plan. Parents/carers are encouraged to talk to their primary school SENDCo and Education Officer supporting the primary school and to contact the Special Educational Needs Support Service (01865 323012).
Students with a Base place are very closely supported by a specialist team of teachers, teaching assistants and outside professionals. Although Base students are attached to mainstream tutor groups, bespoke timetables allow a flexible approach to learning within mainstream lessons, together with more personalised small group and one-to-one work within the Base.
Working with parents/carers, listening to their aspirations and those of their children, to achieve the most appropriate provision, is a key element in all our work.
These short animations explain how a child or young person can get the support and help they need through an Education, Health and Care Plan or an EHC Plan for short:
For enquiries related to SEND students and Faculty staff, at Lower School, please contact the Lower School SEND Administrator on 01844 210715.
For enquiries relating to SEND students and Faculty staff, at Upper School, please contact the Upper School SEND Administrator on 01844 210604.
Our contact email is SENDCO@lordwilliams.oxon.sch.uk.
Mr Robin Whitby, SENDCO/Assistant Headteacher
Named Trustee with Responsibility for SEND: Mrs Rachael Barnard

Trustees and the Thame Partnership Academy Trust
Lord Williams’s School is moving towards a single tier structure for governance, which will now be referred to as the Trust Board:
Three committees will support the work of the Trust Board:
Trustees will normally sit on one Committee, depending on their skills and experience.
For the remainder of the 2025–26 academic year, the Committees will align their work with the current School Improvement Plan (SIP) and monitor a small number of key priorities including preparation for Ofsted. From 2026–27 onwards, the Trust Board will contribute to setting SIP priorities before they are finalised.
Link Trustee roles will align with key priority areas and the renewed Ofsted framework (inclusion, leadership and governance, curriculum and teaching, attendance and behaviour, achievement, personal development and wellbeing, safeguarding and post-16 provision), rather than individual subject areas.
The Board will undertake a review in Autumn 2026 to consider the effectiveness of the Committees, the Board and Link Trustee roles. Governance documentation, including policies, the articles, scheme of delegation and website information, will be updated to reflect the new arrangements.
The Thame Partnership Academy Trust (TPAT) is governed by a Trust Board made up of highly committed individuals who bring a range of skills and experience to ensure robust governance and oversight. The Trustees work together to enable excellent education for all the students at Lord Williams’s School, by providing strategic leadership, support and challenge to the leaders within the Trust. The Academy Trust is a charitable company limited by guarantee with a direct link to the Department for Education (DfE).
The Board of Trustees is overseen by the Members, a number of individuals who do not actively participate in the management of the school but who are responsible for the appointment of trustees and who ensure that management procedures are followed correctly. They also ensure that the school’s ethos is maintained and protected by the Board of Trustees.
The Board of Trustees is responsible to the DfE for the appropriate running of the school within national guidelines and legislation and for ensuring that the money received from the DfE is properly spent. The school also has a Finance, Facilities, Audit and Risk Committee that reviews the school’s financial procedures and its management of the risk register. The trustees prepare annual reports and budgets which have to be approved by both the Charity Commissioners and the DfE.
Trustees may be contacted by getting in touch with the Governance Clerk at the Upper School. Please find below Financial Statements and Key Statutory Documents.
More information about the Board of Trustees and the Committees can be accessed by using the links on the left-hand side of this page.
Please note: The school is currently transitioning from a Governing Body to a Board of Trustees. During this period, some documents and policies may still refer to “governors” as we complete the transition to the new structure.

You will only need to do this once while your child is at this school, unless any information should change. Students cannot attend off site sporting fixtures without a completed consent form.
Cricket Helmets
As the cricket season begins and students take part in training sessions and fixtures, we have reviewed the latest safety guidance issued by the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB).
Following research conducted by the ECB’s Science & Medicine and Recreational Game departments, updated recommendations have been introduced to further improve safety within recreational cricket. This follows evidence that a number of injuries could have been reduced or prevented through enhanced protective equipment.
The ECB now strongly advises that neck protectors are worn whenever helmets are used. A neck protector (also known as a stem guard) is attached to the rear base of the helmet and is designed to reduce the frequency and severity of injuries to the upper rear neck area.
In light of this guidance, and to support student safety and safeguarding, all students participating in hardball cricket at school will be required to wear an ECB-standard helmet fitted with an appropriate neck protector.
While additional neck protectors can be purchased separately, these only meet the guidance when fitted to compatible helmets specified by the manufacturer. For example, Masuri state that their neck guards are only designed for use with selected Masuri helmet models.
To support this requirement, the school has purchased a number of suitable helmets and will continue to add to this provision throughout the year to ensure students can participate safely in both training and matches. Students will not be permitted to use their own helmet unless it meets the required standard and includes the appropriate neck protection.
Thank you for your support and understanding. We hope all students continue to enjoy their cricket at Lord Williams’s safely and successfully.
Richard Beerling, Head of Physical Education
